title: fix: complete the cover letter at the export boundary and repair the pipeline regressions
body:
## The bug

The staged pipeline's letter prompt (`pipeline/resume/prompts.rs`, `letter_system`) tells the model:

> Do NOT write a contact header, a salutation line, or a signature block — **the application adds them at export time**.

The application never did. `parse_cover_letter` only ever *parsed* those parts out of a full letter. The résumé side of the identical promise **is** kept (`validate/mod.rs`, `ContactProfile::apply_to_header`), which is why résumés looked right and letters did not.

Introduced by `19a6de3e` (apply flow → staged pipeline), which deleted the one-shot TS path along with `extractMetadata`, the full-letter prompt, the market-conventions block and company research. Not by the agentic deletion in `93174a1c` — that prompt actually produced complete letters.

### What a real German letter rendered as

| Slot | Should be | Rendered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `letterhead.name` | the candidate | the whole 380-char opening paragraph |
| `date` | 16. August 2026 | a body paragraph containing "0 % auf 90 %." |
| `body` | 3–5 rich paragraphs | **empty** |
| `salutation` / `signoff` | market pair | **absent** |
| `signature_name` | the candidate | the opening paragraph, again |

With no salutation the parser never starts the body, so every paragraph fell into the pre-salutation branch and rendered as recipient lines: plain text, hard line breaks, no bold, no paragraph spacing.

## The fix

`complete_letter_text` synthesises the market salutation, sign-off and signature name for a body-only letter, inserted **after** any leading subject/date furniture. It is called once from `validate_and_normalize`, so PDF, both DOCX scanners and the live preview all inherit it — and **every letter already stored renders correctly with no regeneration**. Verified idempotent, so a full letter still round-trips byte-identically.

Also in scope, because the same cutover caused them:

- **Market etiquette** — `<market_conventions>`, the subject line and an app-supplied date are back in the prompt; the market is resolved from the posting's location, so US postings get US Letter instead of A4.
- **Bold** — the prompts ask for keyword emphasis again (letter *and* résumé draft); `sanitize_markdown` already preserves `**…**`.
- **ATS/quality panel** — `top_requirements` now comes from the `analyze_job` stage rather than the request the tailor surface sends empty. That single change un-starves the requirement metric, stops the empty list freezing the keyword chips through a pick-non-empty merge, and makes `regenerate_section` validate against the same list the run used. The renderer's `meta` is seeded from the aggregate instead of fabricated, which also stops a non-null stub short-circuiting the answers assistant's own extraction.
- **`humanize`** ran after validation with gates that never looked at keyword coverage; it now rejects a rewrite that drops coverage past the existing threshold.
- **Company research** reaches the letter again, opt-in, through the *same* `AI_RESEARCH_BUCKET` rate/concurrency limiter and provider daily ceiling as the existing command — one named constant, one runtime bucket, guard held across the call.
- Predicate hardening: a name is capped at 64 chars / 8 tokens, a date at 48 / 8; the letterhead name falls back to the contact profile before the letter's first line.

## Guardrails

Every existing letter test fed a *complete* letter — the shape the **old** prompt produced. That is exactly why this survived. Added adversarial body-only fixtures carrying the three traps from the real incident (long opening paragraph, digits-and-period paragraph, a bold keyword) plus PDF text-layer and DOCX `document.xml` contract tests, **verified failing** against a neutered `complete_letter_text`. A prompt↔export lock test names the synthesiser that must be retired if the prompt ever stops delegating.

## Verification

`cargo test --lib` 4051 passed · `cargo test --test architecture` 18 · clippy `--all-features -D warnings` clean · `cargo fmt --check` clean · `pnpm test` 6898 passed / 478 files · typecheck 13/13 · `lint:strict --max-warnings 0` clean · `gen:ipc:check` in sync.

Security review found no HIGH/CRITICAL. Its MEDIUM findings are fixed here: a third export path (`GenerationCard`) still sent no locale and would have appended an English salutation to a German letter — a defect this branch introduced — and the new fence assertions were vacuous until the hostile payload was extended to forge the tags it asserts on (mutation-tested red, then green).

## Known gaps, recorded not fixed

Pipeline letters still lose link injection (TS-side, needs porting); tone/mode/applicant-preference conditioning is still absent from the staged letter prompt. The Jobs-page match badge is a cached score of the *saved default* résumé and no surface has ever re-scored it after a generation — making it move is a product decision, not a regression fix.

ADR-034 records the ownership split.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Generate market-aware résumés and cover letters using location, date, tone, and formatting conventions.
  * Optionally research companies for more tailored cover letters, while generation continues if research is unavailable.
  * Use resolved job requirements to improve drafting, validation, and humanization.
  * Preview and export cover letters with consistent locale-specific salutations, sign-offs, signatures, and candidate-name fallbacks.
  * Infer markets from job locations for more accurate previews and PDF/DOCX exports.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of blank names, dates, letter formatting, and export metadata.
  * Reduced sensitive detail in research logs.

* **Documentation**
  * Added cover-letter export behavior documentation.
